chunks.title: Floaters & vitreous haemorrhage
chunks.tldr: Vitreous ~4 ml gel (collagen + hyaluronic acid); never re-forms. Haemorrhage causes: PVD ± tear, proliferative retinopathy (DR, RVO, sickle, Eales), macroaneurysm, trauma, bleeding disorders, Terson. Dense VH → B-scan to rule out RD/melanoma.
points: Muscae volitantes: normal embryological remnants; sudden increase = PVD or bleed.
Mild VH: floaters + haze, VA may be fine. Dense: severe loss.
B-scan: uniform echoes, particulate once clotted.
Low threshold for early vitrectomy in dense VH.
Terson syndrome: intraocular blood with subarachnoid haemorrhage (often ACom aneurysm) or raised ICP; often bilateral; clears in months; good prognosis.

cards.a: Intraocular (retinal/preretinal/vitreous) haemorrhage associated with subarachnoid haemorrhage or acute raised ICP.

cards.q: Essential test in dense vitreous haemorrhage?
cards.a: B-scan ultrasound to exclude RD or tumour.

chunks.title: Asteroid hyalosis vs synchysis scintillans
chunks.tldr: Asteroid: calcium pyrophosphate (calcium soaps) snowballs, unilateral 75%, elderly men, don't sink, rarely affect vision. Synchysis scintillans: cholesterol golden flakes after chronic haemorrhage (blind eyes), sink when eye is still.
points: Asteroid: 3% of 75–86-year-olds; ?diabetes link unproven; bright on OCT/US.
Asteroid + reduced VA → look for second pathology.
chunks.hook: Asteroids float in space; cholesterol sinks like grease.

cards.q: Which vitreous opacity settles inferiorly when the eye is still?

chunks.title: Amyloid, cysts & fetal remnants
chunks.tldr: Familial amyloidosis: 'glass wool' vitreous + polyneuropathy + prominent corneal nerves + light-near dissociation. Cysts: pigmented (ciliary body) or non-pigmented (hyaloid remnant). Remnants: Bergmeister papilla (disc), Mittendorf dot (posterior lens).
points: Amyloid opacities start perivascular, then sheet-like; footplates on lens. Vitrectomy if dense.
Cysts: usually harmless; laser cystotomy/vitrectomy if bothersome.
Persistent fetal vasculature = bigger version (previously PHPV).
Congenital vitreous veil: very rare, no treatment.

cards.a: On the posterior lens capsule (anterior hyaloid artery remnant).
